newsitem.title: CHINA: China bans random charges to ease burden on firms.
newsitem.headline: China bans random charges to ease burden on firms.

text.p: China should ban local governments from forcing state-owned firms to pay unauthorised extra charges as part of efforts to ease the burden on the lumbering state sector, the People's Daily said on Monday.

"At present, the unreasonable burden on firms accounted for 20 percent of pre-tax profits made by state enterprises," the newspaper said, quoting Zhang Wule, vice minister of the State Economic and Trade Commission.
China's state-owned industrial firms reported post-tax profits of 41.7 billion yuan ($5.0 billion) in 1996 while the unauthorised fees charged on such firms were about 60 billion yuan, Zhang said.
In 1995, the extra fees randomly collected by local governments from enterprises were 34.5 billion yuan, he said.
Zhang said government departments could not resolve their capital shortages by collecting extra fees from state enterprises.
About seven percent of state industrial enterprises have stopped or slashed production, resulting in about 7.5 million redundant employees, he said.
About 20 million people worked in loss-making enterprises and most were not receiving their salary on time, he said.
Zhang said local governments should strictly obey a circular issued by the State Council, or cabinet, in early July to halt random charges on state firms.
Inspection groups sent out by the State Council would launch nationwide checks and severely penalise units that do not stop unauthorised extra charges, he said but gave no details of the punishments.
